newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes down, but c.bank defence firm.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes down, but c.bank defence firm.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended slightly lower on Tuesday on active greenback demand, but the central bank's persistent defence prevented the local unit from falling sharply, dealers said.

The local unit traded in a narrow T$28.721-727 range throughout the day before closing at T$28.727 -- the level the central bank has been defending over the past week -- compared with Saturday's T$28.720 close.
The market was closed on Monday because of a typhoon.
Turnover through dealers was heavy at US$403 million.

Dealers said currency jitters in many southeast Asian countries intensified buying on the U.S. currency, but they said the central bank was determined to defend the Taiwan dollar against speculative attacks.

"The central bank has been one of the major U.S. dollar suppliers recently. The central bank is not kidding when it said it has enough bullets to defend the local currency," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Saturday the island, unlike Southeast Asian nations, has huge financial power to defend its currency from foreign speculation.
"Our situation is totally different from Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines and Indonesia," Sheu told a seminar. "Our situation is stable like a mountain. We won't have any problems."
"Foreign speculators intend to manipulate our market, but they also are a little bit scared, because we have enough bullets to defend the Taiwan dollar in a reasonable level," Sheu said.
Dealers said the Taiwan dollar would remain stable.
"The rate will be very stable. It won't go anywhere unless the central bank agrees," the dealer said.
